subject: SLO qualification & next steps — p95/p99 latency targets and test plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@brightedgehealth.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO qualification & next steps — p95/p99 latency targets and test plan

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the BrightEdge Health team. Recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope a brief POC focused on latency/throughput validation: 

Summary from our notes:
- Primary objective: validate Redwood hosted API can meet BrightEdge production SLOs end-to-end (network + app + inference).
- Target SLOs you mentioned on the call: p95 and p99 latency targets for full request lifecycle (client->Redwood->model->client).
- Streaming is desirable for your UX (token-level updates).
- Peak concurrency and replay patterns still TBD — please confirm.

Action items we need from your side to build a test plan:
1) Confirm numeric SLO targets (p95 / p99) you need to validate for go/no-go.
2) Provide representative prompt/response size distribution (avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens, any long-tail cases).
3) Typical arrival pattern (bursty vs steady), target RPS or concurrency we should stress to.
4) Any firewall/allowlist requirements for our test IPs and an API key or sandbox token to run non-prod load.
5) Attach any existing latency reports or a CSV of observed p95/p99 from your current provider.

What we propose from Redwood (short POC):
- Baseline: single-region hosted API, same model family as you use today.
- A/B: run identical traffic against your current provider and Redwood to capture end-to-end p95/p99 under the same load.
- Streaming validation: verify chunked delivery and partial responses at realistic client buffer sizes.
- Deliverables: a short report with p50/p95/p99, tail latency graphs, QPS/concurrency behavior, and suggested config (batching/quantization) if we see regressions.

I've attached a quick "redwood_slo_checklist.xlsx" to show the fields we'll collect. If you can send the numbers in (1)-(4) above, we'll draft a mutually agreed test window.

Proposed next step: 45-minute POC kick-off next Thursday (May 27) 09:00-10:00 PT. Does that work for your team?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: SLO qualification & next steps — p95/p99 latency targets and test plan

Thanks, Karthik — good summary. Quick answers below and I attached our most recent metric export for the current provider.

Requested SLOs (end-to-end):
- p95 <= 250 ms
- p99 <= 450 ms

Current provider observed (last 30 days):
- p95 = 260 ms
- p99 = 480 ms
(see attached current-metrics-2026-05.csv)

Traffic profile and concurrency:
- Typical prompts: median ~45 tokens, mean ~60 tokens.
- Typical responses: median ~140 tokens, mean ~180 tokens.
- Peak concurrency (business-critical workflows): sustained up to ~120 concurrent requests; bursts up to 300 concurrent for 10-30s during batch jobs.
- Arrival pattern: mostly bursty with short hot-windows (we replay batched user uploads).

Streaming: yes — client expects token-by-token delivery for some interactive screens. We need to validate partial-output latency and streaming throughput.

Allowlist and sandbox: we can provision a sandbox API key for testing; procurement will confirm network allowlists. I'll loop them in.

Procurement contact: procurement@brightedgehealth.com

Happy to take the proposed kick-off on Thu 27 May 09:00 PT.

Sarah Nguyen
Director, AI Integrations | BrightEdge Health
sarah.nguyen@brightedgehealth.com

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO qualification & next steps — p95/p99 latency targets and test plan

Appreciate the details, Sarah — that's exactly what we needed. Quick response and plan: 

1) We can target p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 450ms for the hosted API POC. We'll document expected trade-offs and capture tail behavior.

2) For the burst profile you described, we'll run two phases: sustained concurrency at 120 RPS and short bursts that simulate your 300-concurrency spikes. We'll ensure warm cache and cold-start windows are tested.

3) Streaming: we'll validate both chunk size and latency-to-first-byte for streaming responses. Please let us know the client chunking behavior (e.g., send buffer flush every N tokens or time interval).

4) To run A/B we need a sandbox key and an allowlist for these IP ranges (will provide our ephemeral test pool): 34.213.12.0/24, 18.204.56.0/24. If you prefer VPN/VPC peering for the POC, we can accommodate on the Dedicated side but that increases setup time.

5) Proposed test window: May 27-28, run baseline + A/B during low-production traffic (we'll coordinate live traffic cutovers).

Next steps: I'll have Aisha draft the technical test plan and Connor will coordinate scheduling. We'll also drop a one-page mutual action plan in the HubSpot deal for sign-off.

See you on Thu 27 — I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Karthik

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: SRE / test-plan notes for POC (draft)

Hi Sarah — putting a quick technical checklist here so everyone has visibility before the kick-off. I attached a short markdown test plan too. High-level items we'll validate during the POC: 

- Endpoint parity: confirm the same model family and temperature settings for apples-to-apples comparison.
- Warm vs cold: run a warmup phase (5–10 minutes) to populate KV/cache, then capture cold-start percentiles separately.
- Concurrency test: sustained 120 concurrent requests (30m window) + 3x burst tests to 300 concurrent (30s each).
- Throughput: measure RPS, tokens/sec, and CPU/GPU utilization on Redwood side (we'll provide anonymized metrics).
- Streaming metrics: time-to-first-byte (TTFB), time-to-first-chunk, chunk sizes, and client buffer behavior.
- End-to-end: capture client -> network -> model -> client latency; we'll instrument both sides.
- Failure modes: observe graceful degradation and fallback behavior if a node is overloaded.

Tech asks for BrightEdge:
- Sandbox API key + allowlist window for our test IPs.
- Representative payloads (15–50 sample prompts with length distribution).
- Any downstream aggregation that happens on your side (post-processing) that contributes to end-to-end latency.

I'll drop the draft test plan (slo-test-plan.md) into the HubSpot deal and into the Drive link Karthik shared. If you want, Connor can run through the streaming client on the kick-off.

Thanks,
Aisha
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
